reason: Expanding the glacier seems a direct way to bring on the cold age.
expectation: I expect more ice or an advancing ice sheet, though the result may be something else.

effect: The advancing ice establishes the cold conditions; I can now apply them to the recovering world.
reaction: The snowfall explanation makes the ice's gradual advance clear.
reason: This directly brings the advancing ice into contact with the living world.
expectation: I expect the world to enter a colder phase, changing habitats and perhaps revealing ways for life to survive.

alternatives.reason: Variation may help survivors endure, but I want to see the ice age's effects first.

effect: The advancing ice has displaced wildlife, so finding where those animals can go is the next priority.
reaction: The result makes the habitat loss tangible, though it gives little detail.
reason: Rivers may offer displaced animals a route or refuge.
expectation: I expect wildlife to follow the rivers toward a more hospitable habitat, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Variation might help small survivors endure the cold, but I want to follow the displaced wildlife first.

effect: The displaced wildlife has a migration route along rivers; I will now explore another way life can endure.
reaction: The migration follows naturally from the river choice, though the result is brief.
reason: Variation among small survivors may provide another response to the cold.
expectation: I expect a population with traits that help it survive the ice age, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The survivors now have variation that can be tested against the advancing ice.
reaction: The result is plausible but brief; I am curious how the cold affects them.
reason: Combining the varied survivors with the ice may show another way life persists through the cold.
expectation: I expect some survivors to fare better in the cold, though the specific outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Water in the desert might create a refuge, but I want to follow the survivors first.

effect: The survivors now include cold-adapted populations, illustrating selection across generations rather than individual adaptation by choice.
reaction: The explanation usefully clarifies how inherited variation relates to survival.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and water might create a desert refuge.
expectation: I expect water to make a wetter desert habitat, perhaps an oasis, though the result is uncertain.

effect: The desert now has an oasis that may provide a refuge for migrating wildlife.
reaction: The oasis was predictable, but it gives the migration a plausible destination.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may connect the migrating wildlife with a refuge.
expectation: I expect the migrating wildlife to reach or use the oasis, though the exact outcome is uncertain.

effect: The migrating wildlife has a sheltered destination, complementing the populations adapted to cold.
reaction: The emphasis on needing both a route and a suitable destination makes migration's limits clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may bring the two survival paths together.
expectation: I expect a surviving community encompassing both sheltered and cold-adapted populations, though the exact outcome is uncertain.

effect: The refuge and cold-adapted populations have become surviving lineages; the remaining combination may carry them beyond the cold.
reaction: The result joins the two survival paths, though it offers little detail.
reason: This is the only offered combination; fire may represent returning warmth.
expectation: I expect warming conditions to change the survivors' world, though the exact outcome is uncertain.

effect: The warming completes the ice-age journey: survivors spread as ice retreats, but some lineages were lost.
reaction: The ending brings the different survival paths together without treating survival as guaranteed.

mostWorthwhile.text: Creating cold-adapted populations was most worthwhile: it clearly linked inherited variation to survival across generations without implying that individuals adapt by choice.

leastWorthwhile.text: The river migration result was rather brief; it followed naturally from the choice but offered little detail until the oasis appeared.

surprise.text: The sheltered oasis clarified that migration depends on both an accessible route and a suitable destination, not simply the ability to move.

arbitrary.text: Fire combined with surviving lineages felt somewhat symbolic rather than physically clear, although returning warmth made sense as the outcome.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the surviving lineages reshape the world after the ice, although several intermediate results were terse.
